A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PU-learning benchmark, model-selection criteria, and internal-label-shift calibration. Text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments comparing seventeen PU-learning algorithms across four datasets, together with calibration experiments under one-sample and two-sample settings.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark and calibration results in Sections 4–5 and Appendix D, including numerical tables and performance figures.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same augmentation of unlabeled minibatches with positive minibatches. The calibration estimator and PA/PAUC model-selection procedures are unchanged; newly specified backbone details do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-10, ImageNette, USPS, and Letter with the same two positive-class configurations. The one-sample/two-sample scenarios and positive-data sweeps are retained.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same seventeen algorithms and calibrated variants. Dist-PU remains omitted from the ImageNette calibration analysis. The new discussion of concurrent PU-Bench is not an additional evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The reported data configurations, 20,000 SGD iterations, evaluation every 100 iterations, ten hyperparameter configurations per split, selection criteria, and test metrics remain unchanged. v2's architecture specifications supply previously missing details without reporting a protocol revision.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 and Figures 2–3 retain the same investigation of calibration and internal label shift as positive-data amounts vary. No ablation, robustness test, sensitivity analysis, or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report three random data splits and present means and standard deviations. There is no change to repeated-run information, uncertainty-reporting practices, or statistical testing.

E6.justification: All 2,760 mean-and-standard-deviation entries match across the sixteen corresponding result tables, and the figure graphics are unchanged. v1's ImageNette Tables 7 and 9 become v2's Tables 3 and 4 without changing results; the reported findings are also retained.

T1.justification: The definitions, two propositions, two theorems, risk-estimator derivations, and supporting lemma and proofs retain their mathematical content. v1 Appendix A becomes v2 Appendix B, with only formatting and grammatical edits.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the central claims concerning a unified PU benchmark, realistic model selection, internal label shift, and calibration. The conclusion's added 'to the best of our knowledge' qualifier does not materially alter their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Beyond v1's statement that PA requires a known or estimated class prior, v2 Section 3.2 explicitly discusses this limitation, places class-prior estimation outside the paper's scope, and discusses obtaining prior knowledge in applications. Existing result interpretations and the small-dataset limitation remain.

D1.justification: v2 Section 5 adds a PUBench code-location statement and specifies ResNet-34 for image datasets and an MLP with hidden-layer width 500 and ReLU for tabular datasets. v1 named only generic ResNet/MLP configurations in its hyperparameter table. These are documentation additions, not demonstrated experimental changes.

R1.justification: New Appendix A discusses Chen et al. (2026)'s concurrent PU-Bench, distinguishing the present work through its ILS analysis, calibration, and PU-only validation. v2 also adds references for ResNet, ReLU, and the weak-supervision book supporting its class-prior discussion.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are preserved. Local additions include the PA limitation paragraph, concurrent-work appendix, completed nnPU-GA description, acknowledgments, and LLM-use statement, alongside grammatical and author-information edits.

P2.justification: The whole document is retypeset into ICLR conference format, changing typography, headers, spacing, and display sizing and placement. ImageNette result tables move into the main text, the hyperparameter table moves beside implementation details, and appendix figures and tables are arranged together on pages. Existing graphical and numerical content is retained.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses useful documentation gaps by specifying model architectures and adding a code-location statement. Its explicit class-prior scope discussion and acknowledgment of concurrent work improve transparency and research context. These are limited, evidence-supported gains; the methods, proofs, and empirical evidence remain substantively unchanged.
